Article (plain text of the PDF):

Eleven exactly certified violations of the proofreading bound e−2∆
among 88 two-bound-state networks
Verifier-Gated Discovery Lab
Preprint, October 4, 2026
Abstract
Hopfield’s kinetic proofreading scheme [1] has the limiting error rate e−(n+1)∆ for a linear
chain with n proofreading steps. Whether this bound carries over to networks with two
bound states is open: the classification of the enumerated two-bound-state family was not
found in a targeted literature search. We fix ∆ = ln 100 and classify the 88 non-degenerate
rule-compliant two-bound-state topologies. The bound η ≥ e−2∆ is proven for 50 of these
topologies. It is exactly violated for 11, with η < 1e-4 and values down to 1.386398e-12.
For the remaining 27 it is open. For the linear chain with n = 2, η ≥ e−3∆ holds for all
rates. Bounds are proved by symbolic positivity certificates; violations are certified with exact
rational rates. The main limitation is that 27 topologies remain undecided. All violation
certificates lie in a bounded log-rate range.
Keywords: kinetic proofreading, Hopfield bound, error rate, entropy production, Markov
networks, exact certificates

1

Introduction

Kinetic proofreading raises specificity beyond what free-energy differences or kinetic barriers
give, when the reaction is driven strongly but nonspecifically [1]. Error, speed and dissipation
trade off along Pareto fronts, studied analytically and numerically for energy-relay proofreading
[2], generalized Hopfield models [3], and master-equation frameworks [4]. Error bounds fixed by
transition-state energies have been derived for proofreading networks [5, 6]. Several checking
steps can reach a given accuracy at lower dissipation than a single one [7]. Scaling analyses exist
for Hopfield’s original network [8]. Discrimination regimes can include anti-proofreading [9], and
excessive discrimination can remove the nonequilibrium advantage [9].
Open question. Does η ≥ e−2∆ hold for the enumerated two-bound-state topologies, or
can topologies other than the linear chain with one proofreading step go below it?
Contribution. We classify the whole enumerated family with two bound states into proven,
certified-violated and open topologies. The classification uses exact certificates only. A numerical
optimiser serves as a candidate generator.
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows the bound η ≥ e−3∆ for the linear chain with n = 2, for all rates and
fuels.
• Theorem 2 gives a symbolic proof of η ≥ 1/D2 for 50 topologies.
• The next three theorems give exact violations for fam2_66, then for fam2_11 and fam2_9,
then for ten topologies in total.
• The final two theorems give the complete classification (50 / 11 / 27) and the table of exact
error rates.
• Propositions and Examples give supporting statements and exact reachable points for the
linear chain.

Notation. D = e∆ and G = eµ . The error rate is η = JW /JR , the speed is v = JR , and σ is
the entropy production per product in units of kT . These are fixed conventions of the problem
statement.
Family. The verifier’s generator produces 92 rule-compliant two-bound-state topologies. Four
are degenerate (no net production, η = 0/0) and are excluded, leaving 88.

3

Method

Certificate (a), exact reachability. Rational rates (denominator ≤ 106 , log-rates in [−10, 10],
local detailed balance) are inserted into the steady-state equations of a topology. η, σ and v are
evaluated in exact rational arithmetic and compared with the threshold.
Certificate (b), symbolic positivity. A bound η ≥ B is proved by writing η − B = N/D as a
rational function in the rates and in D, G. All coefficients of N and of the denominator must be
nonnegative. The bound then holds for all positive rates and fuel potentials, independent of the
rate range.
Trusted base. The verifier code (exact rational and symbolic arithmetic) is trusted. It passes
a self-test with 18 of 18 cases, comprising true, false, boundary and rule-violation cases. Interval
arithmetic is not part of the certificates reported here. Independent numerical re-searches by the
verifier serve only as counter-checks.
Numerical candidates. Optimizer output, Pareto-front shapes and any value without a
certificate (a) or (b) count only as numerical candidates and carry no result status.
The results were produced by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which every statement
had to pass the code verifier before being kept.

Results

4.1

Main results

Theorem 1 (Hopfield chain, n = 2). For hopfield_n2, η ≥ e−3∆ holds for all positive rates
and all fuel potentials µ, µP ≥ 0.
Certificate. Certificate (b): η − e−3∆ = N/D with 1374 and 2048 terms, all coefficients
nonnegative (check time 6.8 s). Novelty status: not found in a targeted search of 40 abstracts on
2026-10-04. The novelty check classifies this as a reproduction of the Hopfield bound, proved
here rigorously.
Theorem 2 (Proven bound for 50 topologies). For 50 topologies of the verifier-generated family
with at most two bound states (one unbound state, edge catalogue of the model), η ≥ 1/D2 holds
for all positive rates and fuel potentials.
Certificate. Certificate (b), symbolic: the bound is proved for 50 of 50 members. The complete
count is consistent with the later classification. Novelty status: not found in a targeted search of
48 abstracts on 2026-10-04.
Theorem 3 (Exact violation in fam26 6). For fam2_66 there exist rational rates in [e−10 , e10 ]
satisfying local detailed balance with η ≤ 0.0001 and v ≥ 0.0001.

1.4746e-03. The edges of fam2_66 are binding at C0, fuel-driven conversion C0→C1, fuel-driven
discard from C1, and product formation from C1. Novelty status: not found in a targeted search

Supporting statements

Proposition 9 (Enumeration). The generator yields 92 rule-compliant two-bound-state topologies,
of which 4 are degenerate; 88 remain.
Proposition 10 (Early symbolic subfamily). For 3 topologies of the verifier-generated family

sub-e−2∆ error requires a fuel-driven discard exit. Novelty status: not found in targeted searches

Remark. This 3-member list is superseded by the complete list of the theorem on 50 topologies.

5

Negative results
• For 27 topologies, neither a proof of η ≥ e−2∆ nor an exact counterexample was obtained.
These remain open.
• Failed verifier-gated attempts, with their reasons, are recorded in Appendix A.

6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

The linear chain with n = 2 obeys η ≥ e−3∆ for all rates. With two bound states, e−2∆ is violated
exactly by 11 of 88 topologies; the smallest certified error rate is 1.386398e-12, for fam2_43.
The violation in fam2_66 uses a fuel-driven discard edge from the product-forming state, with
σ = 8.341626 kT per product and v = 1.4746e-03. All violation certificates use the rate range
[e−10 , e10 ], whereas the proofs do not depend on it.
Open questions:
(i) What is the status of the 27 open topologies?
(ii) Do all 11 violating topologies contain a fuel-driven discard edge? This is established here
only for fam2_66.
(iii) What are the minimal σ and the maximal v at which each violation occurs? Only η is
tabulated for the topologies other than fam2_66.
(iv) Do the chain bounds for the other chain lengths have symbolic certificates? Only n = 2 is
certified here.

A

Agentic laboratory

The laboratory ran 16 rounds with 14 verified statements and 2 negative results. Every round
was preregistered before the experiment. Preregistration H6 (commit 6184672) preceded the first
5

 run, and later additions are dated. The L2c success criterion (at least 5 counterexamples in one
round) was missed: 2 in round 12, 3 in total. The prior literature search retrieved 2752 sources
(arXiv, Europe PMC, Crossref, citation chain). Of these, 2502 were screened, and 158 findings
had a word quote confirmed in the abstract by code. All 11 classic searches had hits. Round 12
verifier output: certificate (a) passed for 2 of 2 cases.
Agents worked in roles (sparing, numerics, skeptic, theorist, researcher). Their claims passed
through the code verifier, and adversarial counter-checks were run against them. In total 29
counter-checks were made: 5 passed, 12 did not pass, and 12 were not executable.
Negative results.
• Question: does sub-e−2∆ error in the two-bound-state family require a fuel-driven discard
exit at the product state? No claim passed the verifier. All four schranke_familie
attempts failed because of a verifier error that was fixed later.
• Question: further violations among the open topologies. The attempt with 11 cases passed
certificate (a) for 10 of 11. fam2_13 failed because a rate lay outside [e−10 , e10 ] (| log k| =
10.06; derived reverse rates also count).
Pareto-front check. The minimal error rate is non-increasing in σmax , because the feasible set
grows. A reported jump for σ ≥ 8 in hopfield_n1 is therefore an optimizer artefact.
